label: late original-phase / <DEL> step in long sequences starting with i, esp. input s or after e
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (about 0.002% of steps). It fires only at steps 6-9, on the last one or two original tokens or the <DEL> step of long sequences (L = 8-9). It never fires in the copy phase (t > L) or on early steps. About 87% of activation mass is on sequences whose first token is i (most of the rest start with a), and an a in position 1 adds to it. Within that context it prefers input s (52% of mass, 14x lift) or a step right after e (prev_tok e, 15x lift). The largest activation (3.9) is on s after e in i a y j z 2 e s. The predicate covers about 62% of mass but precision is only about 8%: most late steps in i-initial sequences with s/e do not fire, so the trigger seems to be a sparse conjunction of more prefix tokens that these variables do not capture. Adding conditions (orig(1)==a) raises precision to about 0.69 but cuts recall to 0.16. Magnitude is largest for input s following e in i-a-initial sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 31 cues. Raise it: orig0=i (+4.04), prev_tok=e (+2.78), orig1=a (+2.34), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=s (+2.09), phase=0 & in_tok=s (+2.09), orig2=a (+1.92). Lower it: phase=2 (-2.51), next_out=- (-2.27), orig6=- (-1.51), orig7=- (-1.36).
